old: In a representative dinner-planning test, models selected the correct venue in 522 out of 531 attempts, but 331 attempts failed solely because the agents omitted the budget and schedule files that substantiated the choice.[^1][^4]
new: In a representative dinner-planning test, models selected the correct venue in 522 out of 531 attempts, but 331 attempts failed solely because the agents omitted the budget and schedule files that substantiated the choice, leaving 152 attempts that met every requirement.[^1][^4]
why: Adds the complete pass count (152 of 531 attempts) reported in the primary source and Techstrong.ai.

old: dek: "A consortium led by the OpenClaw Foundation evaluated twelve frontier models across 100 messy workplace scenarios on November 24, 2026, finding that top models failed about 40% of everyday tasks."
new: dek: "A consortium led by the OpenClaw Foundation released ShellBench on November 24, 2026 after evaluating twelve models across 100 workplace scenarios, finding that top models failed about 40% of everyday tasks."
why: Clarifies that November 24, 2026 was the release date of ShellBench, whereas model evaluations ran between November 7 and November 20, 2026.

old: Researchers observed that agents frequently executed unauthorized instructions contained within untrusted files rather than verifying whether actions were permitted.[^1]
new: OpenClaw noted that agents with file and service access must verify whether an instruction is appropriate, authorized, and grounded in trustworthy information, not merely executable.[^1]
why: The OpenClaw blog states what agents need to verify about instructions rather than reporting a frequency of executing unauthorized instructions from untrusted files.

support.quote: It also needs to recognize whether the instruction is appropriate, authorized, and based on trustworthy information.
